About.title: About Previously Lab
paragraphs: Previously Lab is an independent open-source lab. We build Previously — a personal AI agent that organizes memory by time: one timeline of episodic slices instead of scattered chat threads. The idea is simple: an agent that remembers your life should remember it the way you do — by when things happened.

The project is MIT-licensed and Git-native. Every memory is a plain markdown file you can read, diff, and own. The agent's self-model evolves in the open, and every recall answer cites the exact time slices it used — no black box, no lock-in.
Previously Lab is run by @likedreamwalker as an open-source project. The best way to follow or join the work is the GitHub repository and the dev.to essay on the memory model, both linked below.

Meta.title: Privacy Policy
Meta.description: What data this site and the Previously playground collect — spoiler: almost none.

sections.heading: This website
sections.body: This site uses Vercel Web Analytics — a privacy-friendly, cookieless counter that gives us anonymous, aggregate numbers only: page views, referrers, and rough geography. It sets no cookies, collects no personal data, and does not track you across sites. There are no tracking pixels and no advertising cookies. The only things stored on your device are your theme preference and, if your browser sends one, your language preference — both kept in your own browser.

sections.heading: The playground demo
sections.body: The playground on this site enforces a per-IP rate limit (20 requests per hour). The counter is held in memory only and is never persisted or shared. When you run a preset, the preset's fixed content is sent to the model provider (DeepSeek) to generate the demo answer. Presets are fixed demonstrations — the endpoint does not accept free-form prompts. Please don't try to put personal data into it.

sections.heading: The Previously agent
sections.body: Previously itself is local-first. Your memory files live in your own environment and your own GitHub repository. This website never sees them, and Previously Lab has no access to them. What the agent sends to a model provider when you run it depends on your own configuration and is governed by that provider's policy.

sections.heading: Questions
sections.body: Questions about this policy? Open a thread on GitHub Discussions — see the contact page for links.
